label: prop:figure-eight-branching-rule
title: Figure-eight character from Young's lattice branching multiplicities
html:
For any partition \lambda \vdash k and substrate parameter q > 1, the Frobenius character of the figure-eight braid 4_1 = \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1 in the irreducible representation \rho_\lambda of H_k(R, q) is determined by three branching multiplicities in Young's lattice:

  \chi(4_1, \lambda)
  = \bigl(f^{\lambda/[3]} + f^{\lambda/[1^3]} - f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]}\bigr)
  \;-\; f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} \cdot h^2

where f^{\lambda/\mu} = |\mathrm{SYT}(\lambda/\mu)| is the number of standard Young tableaux of skew shape \lambda/\mu (equivalently, the number of saturated chains from \mu to \lambda in Young's lattice), and h = q - q^{-1}.

The two components are:

  • a_\lambda = f^{\lambda/[3]} + f^{\lambda/[1^3]} - f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]}: the classical part (the S_k character of the 3-cycle (123) embedded in S_k).
  • b_\lambda = -f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]}: the q-deformation correction, always \leq 0.

Verified to machine precision (< 10^{-12}) against explicit Hoefsmit seminormal matrix computation for all 191 partitions at k = 3 through k = 11.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
